plan.title: Liver 3' tag-seq treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a bulk RNA-seq dataset (12000 genes x 6 samples, 3 treated vs 3 control liver samples, unpaired, single batch) generated with Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq. Because it is a 3' tag-seq library (one read per transcript molecule, no length dependence), standard length-normalization (TPM/FPKM using gene body length) is not appropriate — DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization on raw counts is the correct approach and needs no gene-length correction. The plan: (1) QC the raw counts and metadata to confirm sample-condition mapping and filter low-count genes, (2) run DESeq2 differential expression with a simple ~condition design (single batch, unpaired, no covariates to adjust for), applying apeglm/ashr shrinkage for stable fold-change estimates given n=3/group, (3) enrich the DE gene list against human pathway databases (WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome) to interpret the treatment's biological impact on liver. All steps operate on human (Homo sapiens, taxon 9606) data and use human-specific reference gene sets available in the environment.
